newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt, Iran in first high-level talks in years.
newsitem.headline: Egypt, Iran in first high-level talks in years.

text.p: Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak met Iran's Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati in Cairo on Tuesday for high-level talks after years of strained relations between the countries.
Velayati's visit was the first by a high-ranking Iranian official since 1994. Iran severed ties with Cairo after Egypt signed a peace treaty with Israeli in 1979.
Ties were further soured by Egyptian charges that Iran supported Moslem radicals in Egypt and was behind an attempt to kill Mubarak in 1995.
Velayati said the main purpose of his visit was to give Mubarak an invitation by Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani to attend an Islamic summit in Tehran in December.

Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa said it was too early to say if Mubarak would attend. He said Egyptian-Iranian relations were at the stage of "discussions and honesty" but they were not talking yet about reestablishing full diplomatic ties.
"It has to be a bilateral will to take that decision," Moussa said. "When the decision will be taken at the right moment it will be taken."

Iran has a low-level diplomatic presence in Egypt, which has accused Tehran and Sudan of supporting the al-Gama'a al-Islamiya (Islamic Group), the largest organisation fighting for a strict Islamic state in Egypt. Sudan and Iran deny this.
Iran was also accused of being behind the attempted assassination of Mubarak during his visit to Ethiopia in 1995.
"We reiterate that this is a baseless allegation against Iran," Velayati said after the meeting.
Asked if there was any response to allegations that Iran supported terrorism, Moussa said: "All of these issues were discussed."

"The results were good and I think a chance to discuss several issues that are of concern to both countries and to the Islamic world and the region. And frankly as a whole it was positive," Moussa said.
"The president has received the invitation and thanked the foreign minister for the message and the discussion was very good, very detailed," he said.
"It was a good opportunity to exchange views at that level with the president...and talk about the situation in the region in a very frank way."
Velayati last visited Cairo in 1994 to attend a Non-Aligned Movement meeting of foreign ministers and a United Nations population conference.

Velayati said Islamic countries had to work together to face problems in the Middle East and Islamic world: "We have a lot of issues that we have to discuss together so this meeting was very frank and we believe it was constructive."
